title: Please don't tell the truth
desc:
Group 3 of the Russian Advisory Group in Afghanistan, Badakhshan, 25 December 1976
"We're not here to win, we're just here to keep it burning."
________________________________________
6:12 a.m
He woke up in the camp room where the electric fan was buzzing, the dust on the floor, and the intermittent coughing sound coming from next door. He forgot who he was a
colonel and what class of outstanding graduates he was. All he remembered was dreaming last night that his wife was feeding soup to his son, who was five years old, but he
had never seen a real person.
Today's mission is to assess the local Allied camp in the D-7 area, a semi-militia organization whose loyalty exists only until the check arrives. The order given to him
by the headquarters was: "Encourage it to confront the German-backed Hazra faction, while ensuring that the threshold of intensification in the theater is not triggered." ”
He got into the jeep, the tires creaking on the gravel like bones running over the sand.
________________________________________
10:44 a.m
The mission arrived at the camp. The "commander" of the camp was a small Afghan leader in his twenties, wearing a Russian-made beret and his clothes were stained with oil.
The translator handed over a letter of funding from headquarters, and his eyes immediately lit up.
The colonel knew that the money was not enough to repair the old Soviet mortars, but he still encouraged the other party with a smirk: "We believe in your struggle. ”
The translator flipped through the pages. He didn't pull out the phrase "this is a meat grinder", nor did he pull out the fact that the colonel didn't say "you can live
for three months at most".
________________________________________
2:35 p.m
The advisory group inspected the barracks, ammunition depots and a small hospital. The taste inside made him gag: there was no anesthetic, only fire and wine and
screaming; There was no gauze, only shredded old newspapers. He saw a fourteen-year-old boy lying on a hospital bed, his belly wrapped in a strip of cloth held in place
with a rope, and the corners of his mouth foamed at the mouth.
The boy tried to raise his head and whispered something. The colonel looked down and listened, and the translator hesitated: "He said, you are from that ...... A place in
paradise? ”
The colonel did not answer. He just turned around and walked out of the tent and threw up outside the door.
________________________________________
6:00 p.m
On the way back, their convoy was overturned by an improvised bomb, and the young non-commissioned officer sitting in the passenger seat died on the spot, with half of his
face cut off. The radio in the car was blown up, and after briefly contacting HQ, I only got one response:
"Record the coordinates and send a helicopter tomorrow morning to recover the body. You continue to follow the route. ”
The colonel sat next to the corpse, speechless all the way. He opened the briefcase, which contained the "Loyalty Assessment Report of Local Forces in Afghanistan" written
by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with a five-level score, complete charts, and bright and eye-catching red and blue colors. He closed the papers, his face smiling for
the first time in more than a dozen days.
It was a world-weary sneer.
________________________________________
10:58 p.m
The advisory group returned to base. Dinner was cold canned and boiled carrots. The colonel washed his face and lay down. Wind and sand blew in through the broken window,
and he didn't have the strength to close it.
Before the lights went out, he flipped out his communication log and recorded an audio report:
"Group 3 has completed its mission. Camp D-7 is in a manageable state and is expected to maintain combat effectiveness for more than three months without significant
external intervention. No anomalies. ”
He hesitated for a moment, and finally added:
"Everything works."
End of recording. He closed his eyes and dreamed that his son asked him, "Dad, who did you protect today?" ”

title: How long are we going to stay?
desc:
Armed Forces of the Republic of Russia, 11th Infantry Brigade, 2nd Company, Paktia Front, Afghanistan, May 8, 1977
________________________________________
4:12 a.m
They woke up with a cough. The cold wind crept through the gaps in the sandbags, and the roof of the tent dripped with ice water that had melted last night. Private Andrei
Sherepin curled up in a blanket, staring at the rusty iron beams overhead. He doesn't remember how many days he's been in the sand, only that the last time HQ sent a
condolence package was last autumn — the cans inside were swollen.
"How long are we going to stay?"
He whispered to his partner Nemtsov. The other party didn't answer, just wiped the frozen blood on the loader with a broken towel.
HQ did not tell them whether they were still "on the front line" - because there was no rear here anymore.
________________________________________
10:20 a.m
Today we will patrol in shifts to the southern section of Highway 7, a "death zone" that even the guerrillas do not want to approach. One team went missing there, and a
week later, their uniforms were nailed to the burned-out school bus.
The commander handed over a map with blurred ink circles on three possible IED burial areas in red pen, and then threw down the following sentence:
"Be careful, or your mother won't even be able to receive the ashes."
Andrei put on his helmet, grabbed his rifle, and followed the group in silence.
________________________________________
1:03 p.m
They found a landslide in the second area. Something was buried in the dirt, revealing a black sole. André approached cautiously and lifted the sand, revealing a shattered
corpse. It's not the Russian army, it's the remnants of some local armed soldier with an American first-aid kit on him.
"Hell knows which side he is."
Nemtsov spat and moved on.
Andrei stood for a moment, silently placing an empty kettle on the corpse's chest. He didn't know why he did it. Maybe it's just to let the people "over there" know that
there are still people alive here and what else can be done.
________________________________________
6:41 p.m
On their return to the camp, they were briefly ambushed - three of their companions were shot, one of whom was a new recruit who had just been transferred from Siberia for
three months. When Andrei knelt on the ground to bandage him, the boy kept staring at him, and the blood on his face made him tremble when he spoke:
"Brother...... Does HQ know we're here? ”
Andrei did not answer. He held down the artery, watched the blood come out of his fingers, and the words echoed in his heart over and over again: How long are we going to
stay?
________________________________________
11:08 a.m
The camp was as quiet as a grave. The radio began to broadcast the dead propaganda tape again: "Every inch of Afghanistan is the front line of our defense of civilization
" ”
Andre was lying on the bed, but his mother's voice sounded in his head: "Remember to go home." ”
He took out the letter from under his pillow, which he could no longer read, read it again, and then lit it with a broken match.

4:12 a.m
They woke up with a cough. The cold wind crept through the gaps in the sandbags, and the roof of the tent dripped with ice water that had melted last night. Private Andrei
Sherepin curled up in a blanket, staring at the rusty iron beams overhead. He doesn't remember how many days he's been in the sand, only that the last time HQ sent a

"How long are we going to stay?"
He whispered to his partner Nemtsov. The other party didn't answer, just wiped the frozen blood on the loader with a broken towel.
HQ did not tell them whether they were still "on the front line" - because there was no rear here anymore.
________________________________________
10:20 a.m
Today we will patrol in shifts to the southern section of Highway 7, a "death zone" that even the guerrillas do not want to approach. One team went missing there, and a
week later, their uniforms were nailed to the burned-out school bus.
The commander handed over a map with blurred ink circles on three possible IED burial areas in red pen, and then threw down the following sentence:
"Be careful, or your mother won't even be able to receive the ashes."
Andrei put on his helmet, grabbed his rifle, and followed the group in silence.
________________________________________
1:03 p.m
They found a landslide in the second area. Something was buried in the dirt, revealing a black sole. André approached cautiously and lifted the sand, revealing a shattered
corpse. It's not the Russian army, it's the remnants of some local armed soldier with an American first-aid kit on him.
"Hell knows which side he is."
Nemtsov spat and moved on.
Andrei stood for a moment, silently placing an empty kettle on the corpse's chest. He didn't know why he did it. Maybe it's just to let the people "over there" know that
there are still people alive here and what else can be done.
________________________________________

three months. When Andrei knelt on the ground to bandage him, the boy kept staring at him, and the blood on his face made him tremble when he spoke:

stay?
________________________________________

" ”
Andre was lying on the bed, but his mother's voice sounded in his head: "Remember to go home." ”

title: We never promise tomorrow
desc:
CIA Afghanistan Task Force, suburb of Herat, July 4, 1978
________________________________________
06:03 - Daily launch of the codename "Katrina".
The pump is broken. He washed his face with sand water again, and the dust on his face became thicker and thicker. The CIA's "Observation Outpost" is disguised as an aid
medical facility, with a façade painted in light blue of OFN-OAS, and two Pashto-speaking "doctors" standing at the door, both with M1911 hidden behind them.
He used a fake passport, a fake name, and a fake life. What his last name is, no one cares anymore. His mission designation is K-3/208/A, or "Katrina" for short, which is
more important than his name.
________________________________________
08:45 - meeting the "freedom fighters"
What I want to meet today is the "asset" raised by the CIA itself - "Mohammad Lakim", the small leader of a local anti-Russian armed force. HQ demanded a new batch of
ammunition and communications equipment, as well as an exchange of "topographical information on the activities of Russian advisers."
Lakim was an hour late. He brought with him an icy plastic box containing the heads of two captured Russian soldiers. He also joked, "If you give me more ammo, I'll be
able to save your whole face next time." ”
He smiled. K-3 did not.
He just nodded and said, "We'll think about it." ”
HQ wants them to "keep the relationship" and not "scare away friends".
________________________________________
13:22 - Communication break logs 47th
At one point, HQ's encrypted radio station went missing for 42 minutes. He sat alone on the rooftop smoking a cigarette, looked over the sand net on the roof, and saw
children playing with empty shells as building blocks in the distance.
They laughed as loudly as they did on the streets of California. But he knew that the fathers of these children were either rotting in the sand or were trained to die by
the kind of "Lakim".
Instinctively, he held up his binoculars to see better, but when he saw one of the children wearing an old T-shirt with the "Pepsi-Cola" motif, he suddenly felt a wave of
nausea.
________________________________________
17:10 - Operation "Wrap Up" fails
He was tasked with confirming the successful disposition of a "target" - a local liaison suspected of leaking secrets to the Russians. Local militants said they had "been
disposed of," but photos from the scene showed that the bodies did not match.
He tried to call the contact point in Kabul and was told: "HQ doesn't care about that line anymore and resources are tilting towards Kandahar." ”
This means that the person may still be alive, and he ...... will never know.
________________________________________
22:39 - log update and burndown
He turned on the small tape recorder he had brought with him. Press the record button. The voice is low and slow:
"Mission No. K-3/208/A, day ninety-six. Failed to identify the target killed. Maintain cooperation with local armed forces, and there are no hostile incidents. It is
proposed to postpone the distribution of the third batch of supplies, and Lakim's intentions are unknown. …… Task Execution Status: Normal. ”
He turned off the recording. He then pulled out several slips of paper from the file bag, containing identity information, intelligence sources, and financial movements.
He lit them with a lighter, threw them one by one into the old iron bucket, and watched the flames lick his life on the papers.
His life was like these documents – living in one-off messages, burned and no longer existing.
________________________________________
01:18 - monologue
He stared at the ceiling, unable to sleep. There will always be a classic sentence in the ears of HQ training:
"We never promise tomorrow, we only honor today's order."

title: From Tokyo to Herat
desc:
Japanese Near East Dispatch Force, Herat, September 18, 1979
________________________________________
At dawn, the blood-colored dawn
Fujita stood at the edge of the camp, staring at the dusky desert in the distance. The morning air was still heavy, with a strong smell of sand and dust, and he habitually
raised his hand to cover the sun in front of him. The sky of Herat is vast, but the vast desert is always suffocating. He put down the telescope in his hand, and the
corners of his mouth curled slightly: "Maybe, this is my fate." ”
Since the order was issued by Tokyo, Japan's Near East Dispatch Army has appeared like a ghost in this "imperial graveyard". Fujita does not deny that he did not come here
for the sake of "freedom" or "justice" – he was here to defend the interests of the empire, to hold the boundaries of power that had been eroded by Japan on a global
scale. War, for Fujita, has long ceased to be a pan-Asianist romance, but a mechanized chess game.
________________________________________
At 9:30 a.m., the tide of battle remained unshaken
"Your task is to provide them with assistance and support their combat effectiveness." Fujita did not have a trace of expression on his face when he conveyed the
instructions of his superiors to his subordinates. The Japanese military's position is clear – to support pro-Japanese forces in Afghanistan and to ensure that the
situation here is not biased in favor of Russia or Western countries. However, the reality is more complex than any strategy.
Every time he interacts with the Afghan armed forces, Fujita feels an inexplicable sense of oppression. The eyes of the soldiers armed in these places were full of
confusion and anger. The land of Afghanistan will not easily accept foreign invaders, regardless of their appearance. In his interactions with these locals, Fujita sensed
their fears and their dislike for Japan's history, the empire that invaded China and Southeast Asia.
Still, he firmly believes, "This place has to be controlled by us." It was for the sake of the "greater future", for the sake of the Japanese Empire to which he was loyal.
________________________________________
At 2:00 p.m., the atmosphere was heavy
Soon after, Fujita received orders to lead his troops to a village south of Herat to provide support. Through intelligence, they learned that pro-Soviet forces in the
region were active and that tough measures had to be taken. However, this is not a simple battle.
There was a suffocating atmosphere in the village. Fujita and his men made their way through the crowd and into a humble dwelling. Inside, several ragged villagers bowed
their heads and remained silent, their eyes uneasy. Fujita couldn't help but realize that the eyes of these villagers were full of fear of war, but more often than not, a
deep rejection of outside forces.
"Our mission is not for the people here." Fujita whispered to the lieutenant accompanying him, "This is just so that Japan's influence will not be weakened." ”
What he didn't say was: "After all, we are just pawns of the empire." ”
________________________________________
6:15 p.m., silence in the cold wind
Back at camp, Fujita stood outside the tent and felt the cold wind from Herat blowing in the desert. This is a picture that has been repeated every day since he arrived in
Afghanistan. Anxiety and tension during the day are accompanied by deep loneliness at night. Despite the hundreds of troops and colleagues around him, Fujita knew that
they all had the same sense of depression in their hearts - this was a war with no winners, and they were nothing more than a group of unchosen warriors trapped in this
desert.
He recalls his time in Tokyo, the glory and dreams of the past, the high spirits of the former Japanese Empire, and everything seems so hopeful. But now, he faces a land
of death and despair, and every inch of Afghanistan is making him lose himself.
Fujita stood for a moment, then jerked around and walked into the depths of the camp.
He clearly knew that he, like all the soldiers on this battlefield, had long since left the so-called "glory" and entered a reality full of mud and blood. And all this,
perhaps, can never be clearly explained, and it is impossible to really stop.
________________________________________
12:00 p.m., the struggle in my heart
As the night wore on, the lights in the camp were gradually extinguished. Fujita lay on a simple bed, his eyes fixed on the roof of the tent. Through the faint light, he
could see the crooked shadows—he knew there was no way back. It was not just for the sake of winning or losing the war, but also for the future of the Japanese Empire, or,
for the fate that he now had to face.
"What is the point of my coming here?" Fujita asked silently in his heart.
No one answered him, and his heart slowly grew cold. Perhaps, this is the truth of war-"

title: Like a ghost
desc:
Co-Prosperity Sphere Observer Group in Afghanistan, Secret Service Unofficial Contact, Herat, 8 May 1980
________________________________________
8:10 a.m
He walked through the dust and sand of the streets and the orange morning light, not fast or slow. Beneath you is the scene of an explosion that was dealt with just
yesterday. The secret service left no traces, only the conclusion: "Non-Chinese assets accidentally touched the misleading materials laid by the United States." ”
He wore a round hat and gray civilian clothes, and hid among merchants, clergy, and advisors. No one knows his name, only one code name: Hiyama No. 2. This is the name of
Tokyo, not Herat.
He walked into a teahouse. The landlord had already left a letter under the counter, the letter was written in Turkish, but the paper was the "silkworm white type"
characteristic of East Asian paper mills. He didn't open the letter, just ordered a cup of black tea, drank it, and left.
________________________________________
11:47 a.m
He met with the nephew of a local pro-Japanese warlord at an abandoned French-style church on the outskirts of Herat.
"We need your people to control that drain." Hiyama whispered, "It's not for irrigation, it's for the three villages on the map." ”
"The Germans are also bidding." The nephew reminded him.
"They're giving money." Hiyama smiled, "What we give is the future. The future of Greater East Asia. ”
The other party was silent for a moment, then nodded. The pledge he signed was sealed in a silver cigarette case and will be sent to Kabul tomorrow morning in a truck,
where it will be returned to Tokyo in a diplomatic package.
Everything was silent, but it was horribly clean.
________________________________________
3:20 p.m
Hiyama walks into the information room behind the Japanese "Cultural Support Center". It was dimly lit and filled with listening tapes and photographs. A young man brought
a new volume of recordings — a phone call between a U.S. military adviser and a Tajik commander in Mazar-i-Sharif, intermittent, but sufficient.
"It is confirmed, the US side is ready to withdraw from the 6th contact point." The young man whispered.
Hiyama didn't answer. He stared at a line on the cassette case: "Sound doesn't necessarily say everything, silence is the dictionary of emotions." ”
He took out his pen and wrote on the intelligence receipt: Point B detection complete. Prepare to carry out local public opinion infiltration.
He added in his heart a sentence that no one heard: war does not need explosions, war is emotion.
________________________________________
6:05 p.m
It was getting dark, and the sunset light in the yellow sand was burning over Herat. He walked back to his lodgings, a small room that had been secretly converted behind
an abandoned warehouse. A local kid squatted at the door and handed him a small folded note.
"Who gave it to you?" He asked.
The child shakes his head.
The note had five letters written on it: "IZNNO". It is the code name for the "involuntary defector" in the old intelligence system of the Tokyo headquarters. Someone is
selling out information - but their own people.
He sat down, didn't turn on the light, just stared at the note until it was dark.
________________________________________
11:11 p.m
He recorded a tape of the debriefing, and his voice was as calm as water:
"The Herat Observation continues to advance. Abwehr tried to circumvent the joint agreement's intelligence-sharing mechanism for the third time this week, and U.S.
advisers had unclear intentions to retreat. The J-3 team may have leaked the secrets and is investigating. The psychological state remains stable. ”
He paused, looking at the old saber on the table.
It was left by my father - a relic of the old empire.
He whispered something that wasn't recorded on tape:
"We're not ghosts anymore, but we haven't learned to be human yet."
________________________________________
He closed the tape recorder, put his hat back on, and walked into the night.

title: Thirteenth signature
desc:
Advisory Mission of the Russian Federation in Afghanistan, Diary of Operations R-7 in the Theater of Operations, April 1, 1981
Location: Nangarhar Province, on the periphery of the buffer zone in southern Ghazni
________________________________________
2:06 a.m
When he opened his eyes, he was still sitting at the aluminium war table, mud on his boots, dirt on his trouser legs, and his fingers still clutching the bitten pen.
The folder was spread out, and the red cover was printed with nine black letters: "Letter of Authorization for Chemical Cleanup Operations".
He had already signed a similar order twelve times.
Today is the thirteenth time.
But he didn't put pen to paper for a long time.
The radio in the corner of the table was also broadcasting a headquarters briefing: "We must quickly weaken the armed will of the south and cut off its logistical contacts
with the German side." The tone was as smooth as the weather forecast.
He closed his eyes and saw only the video sent yesterday - the crowd at the entrance of the village, the guerrillas mixed with the refugees, the children lining up with
empty pots to get water, and a woman holding the child screaming at the camera.
She speaks Pashto. But he understood.
She was scolding them, "Where is your God? ”
________________________________________
9:40 a.m
The airdrop is complete. The flight unit, codenamed "Igor", dropped four tanks of improved CL-34 gas. According to intelligence, more than 60 unarmed civilians were in the
targeted area with suspected guerrillas.
"It's not very likely." The deputy consultant wrote in the report.
"A necessary price." The chief of staff said from the side.
He stood in front of the remote monitoring platform, staring at the white mist wafting out, his palm pressed against the cold glass surface. The drone's picture begins to
blur, with noise, flickering, and finally black and white.
He knew that there was no longer a sound of breathing.
________________________________________
1:22 p.m
Lunch was canned, dry cakes, and sugar water.
He didn't move.
"Do you know what the U.S. military did in Kandahar?" One young consultant said, "We don't even do a hundredth of what they do." ”
He did not respond. Just put his hand in the pocket of his military coat and pinched the carbon paper—it had his signature on it, thirteenth.
The handwriting is more stable than the previous twelve.
That's what makes him sick the most.
________________________________________
6:04 p.m
HQ issued a commendation: "The R-7 acted quickly and decisively, effectively deterring the local armed activity. It is recommended that the authority for asymmetric
operations be continuously expanded. ”
He sat on the slope at the back of the camp, looking out at the valley in the distance, which had been labeled "neutral" by military intelligence. The wind blew from the
mountain pass, with a faint sour smell. He didn't know if it was a real gas residue or a hallucination in his own nasal cavity.
"You didn't do anything wrong." The adjutant said, "It was HQ who asked us to do this." ”
He suddenly asked, "Who is HQ?" ”
The adjutant was stunned.
"Have you ever seen HQ's face? Do you know if HQ has a wife? Do they also dream of those charred bodies in the middle of the night? ”
He paused, and his voice was extremely soft:
"I don't want to dream of that well anymore."
________________________________________
11:59 a.m
He finally returned to the tent and took out the carbon paper one by one, a copy of each order. Twelve are complete, and the thirteenth still bears fingerprints.
He began to burn them one by one.
The light of the fire reflected the tent like a tomb. He knelt on the sand, the last one unburned—"...... Authorized to immediately carry out the clean-up ......" The line

description:
Advisory Mission of the Russian Federation in Afghanistan, Diary of Operations R-7 in the Theater of Operations, April 1, 1981
Location: Nangarhar Province, on the periphery of the buffer zone in southern Ghazni
________________________________________
2:06 a.m
When he opened his eyes, he was still sitting at the aluminium war table, mud on his boots, dirt on his trouser legs, and his fingers still clutching the bitten pen.
The folder was spread out, and the red cover was printed with nine black letters: "Letter of Authorization for Chemical Cleanup Operations".
He had already signed a similar order twelve times.
Today is the thirteenth time.
But he didn't put pen to paper for a long time.
The radio in the corner of the table was also broadcasting a headquarters briefing: "We must quickly weaken the armed will of the south and cut off its logistical contacts
with the German side." The tone was as smooth as the weather forecast.
He closed his eyes and saw only the video sent yesterday - the crowd at the entrance of the village, the guerrillas mixed with the refugees, the children lining up with
empty pots to get water, and a woman holding the child screaming at the camera.
She speaks Pashto. But he understood.
She was scolding them, "Where is your God? ”
________________________________________
9:40 a.m
The airdrop is complete. The flight unit, codenamed "Igor", dropped four tanks of improved CL-34 gas. According to intelligence, more than 60 unarmed civilians were in the
targeted area with suspected guerrillas.
"It's not very likely." The deputy consultant wrote in the report.
"A necessary price." The chief of staff said from the side.
He stood in front of the remote monitoring platform, staring at the white mist wafting out, his palm pressed against the cold glass surface. The drone's picture begins to
blur, with noise, flickering, and finally black and white.
He knew that there was no longer a sound of breathing.
________________________________________
1:22 p.m
Lunch was canned, dry cakes, and sugar water.
He didn't move.
"Do you know what the U.S. military did in Kandahar?" One young consultant said, "We don't even do a hundredth of what they do." ”
He did not respond. Just put his hand in the pocket of his military coat and pinched the carbon paper—it had his signature on it, thirteenth.
The handwriting is more stable than the previous twelve.
That's what makes him sick the most.
________________________________________
6:04 p.m
HQ issued a commendation: "The R-7 acted quickly and decisively, effectively deterring the local armed activity. It is recommended that the authority for asymmetric
operations be continuously expanded. ”
He sat on the slope at the back of the camp, looking out at the valley in the distance, which had been labeled "neutral" by military intelligence. The wind blew from the
mountain pass, with a faint sour smell. He didn't know if it was a real gas residue or a hallucination in his own nasal cavity.
"You didn't do anything wrong." The adjutant said, "It was HQ who asked us to do this." ”
He suddenly asked, "Who is HQ?" ”
The adjutant was stunned.
"Have you ever seen HQ's face? Do you know if HQ has a wife? Do they also dream of those charred bodies in the middle of the night? ”
He paused, and his voice was extremely soft:
"I don't want to dream of that well anymore."
________________________________________

He finally returned to the tent and took out the carbon paper one by one, a copy of each order. Twelve are complete, and the thirteenth still bears fingerprints.
He began to burn them one by one.
The light of the fire reflected the tent like a tomb. He knelt on the sand, the last one unburned—"...... Authorized to immediately carry out the clean-up ......" The line
struggled in the fire, as if begging for mercy.
He finally cried.
Not because of remorse.
Because he knew he would sign the fourteenth.

title: German Air Force Volunteer Corps · Afghanistan Theater · Tactical Pilot Action Log
desc:
June 1, 1982 · Badakhshan region, area of REGEN-E operation
________________________________________
06:04
When he opened his eyes, there was blood outside the window.
No, it's the rising sun. But his first reaction was the orange color after the alarm light flashed. He couldn't figure it out anymore.
On the sheets were salt stains from the sweat he had done last night. In the dream, there was a house that was on fire, and a figure fell from the roof, holding a baby in
his hand. He woke up with his hands clenched, as if he was still trying to hold on to something.
He sat up, his throat tight.
The captain told him that today's mission was just a "regular sweep". Clearing of guerrilla transit points in a certain mountainous area.
"There are no civilians," said the captain, "where are the civilians?" Did you see those radio navigators? It's just a bunch of cowsheds. ”
________________________________________
08:12
Launch. He turned on the HUD, and the system calmly listed the coordinates of the target, the state of the weapon, the wind speed.
He began to pray that something was wrong. At least then he can fly off. Unfortunately, everything works fine.
"In the REGEN-E area, the enemy is expected to be transferred at the western entrance of the K valley and destroy all structures."
He saw the crowd as he swooped.
Not soldiers. Not partisans.
It's a group of people. An old man, a child, a woman was washing clothes by the river, and a child was standing on a stone and waving at him.
He froze. Hand over the release key. The brain stops working.
A reprimand came from the communication channel:
"What are you waiting for? We don't want to take back the baby Madonna, the pilot, to carry out your orders. ”
He pressed it.
He pressed.
________________________________________
08:16
In the dust from the explosion, he saw the child's hand—and in that moment, he did.
But when I looked again, the child was gone. There was just a pile of charred and blackened coals.
He suddenly wondered if he had misremembered.
"Perhaps...... The kid was somewhere else. ”
But a voice echoed coldly in his head: You killed him with your own hands.
________________________________________
13:00
Afternoon. He returned to the base. The officer came over and patted him: "The task was done neatly, cleanly, precisely. ”
The corners of his mouth twitched, and he nodded.
No one mentioned the child. No one mentioned the woman.
Their names, he never known.
________________________________________
15:25
He sat outside the barracks, the sun falling on his knees. He suddenly remembered that his mother was a washerwoman when she was young, and that she knelt by the river to
rub her clothes exactly like the woman this morning.
He covered his face with his palm. That's not self-blame. It was some kind of deeper fear.
- What if he killed his own mother? Own children? Your own neighbors?
But he immediately retorted to himself: "But they are not." They are supporters behind enemy lines, potential threats, saboteurs of imperial security. ”
He took a deep breath.
Then he saw a figure approaching, a girl in a red dress, with dark skin and no shoes on her feet. She walked slowly, step by step.
He slammed to his feet—nothing. The camp was empty.
His back was soaked with sweat.
________________________________________
18:46
He lay in bed, unable to sleep. Fingers grasp the fabric little by little on the side of the pillow.
There was a knock on the door. He got up and opened it, and there was no one outside the door.
He turned around, and there was a child sitting on the bed. Black hair, big eyes, gray all over, holding a broken ball in his hand.
He glared at the child. The kid stared at him too.
Time stood still for a full twenty seconds.
He slammed the light on.
Nothing.
Nothing.
________________________________________
21:10
He wrote his last words in his diary:
"We thought we were dropping bombs, but in fact we were bones."
He put down his pen and looked out the window at the starry sky.
A meteor streaked by.
He instinctively prayed, "If there are gods, let me never see them again in my dreams." ”
But he knew that the god might have died in that village.
Or maybe just lie on the edge of the blown up well, with your eyes still open, looking at him...

title: Under the sand, the rose has not bloomed
desc:
October 10, 1983 · Northern Valley of Badakhshan · The 7th guerrilla stronghold of the Afghan National Liberation Front
________________________________________
04:26
When he woke up, the sky was still dark. The ground was as cold as stone. He pulled his hand from under the blanket, his fingers frozen stiff. The gun rested beside him,
and he subconsciously shook it - the metal was as cold as a knife. He didn't move, and after holding it for a while, it seemed that he could still feel some blood flowing.
Not far away was Hamid, curled up in a broken carpet and coughing. They lost a supply point last night, and only four escaped. The other ten were either dead or didn't
know where they had gone.
Someone called his mother's name in a dream and whimpered in a low voice. When he thought of his mother, he noticed that his face was wet.
But not because of crying, but because there is blood in the dream and a baby crying. He knelt in the rubble, his hands covered with broken bones. He couldn't save the
child.
________________________________________
06:02
They planted explosives in the mountain passes and prepared to ambush a Russian supply convoy.
He deftly tied the lead with his fingers and bit the stem of hay in his mouth. He suddenly laughed.
Hamid asked, "How?" ”
"I also played with these lines when I was a kid...... At that time, I was making kites at home. Now, I'm still making kites. ”
Hamid didn't laugh, just looked at him: "You're crazy. ”
He nodded, "Maybe." ”
________________________________________
10:18
The mine exploded.
Their ambush was successful, but at an extremely high cost. At the moment of the explosion, he stood too close and was stunned. When I woke up, there was scorched earth
all around. The three team members lay down, not moving. One of his heads was broken, and his eyes were still looking at him. It was Rashid, who was only eighteen years
old.
He looked up, and there was a living one in the distance, leaning against the stone and gasping. He rushed over, only to find that it was a Russian soldier, with blood all
over his face, half of his teeth missing, and a song in his mouth.
He raised his gun and aimed it at him.
The man looked up, the corners of his mouth twitching, and he seemed to say, "Mom." ”
He froze.
He fired.
He killed a man who sang and said "Mommy".
________________________________________
14:30
They returned to their hiding place, and it began to snow.
He sat by the fire, roasting his frozen hands.
The firelight flickered. He saw the Russian soldier sitting across from him.
He raised his gun again, only to find that the muzzle of the gun was rusty. There was blood sticking to the trigger, whether it was his own or someone else's, he couldn't
tell the difference.
The soldier spoke, and it was still the same sentence: "Mom." ”
He closed his eyes, and when he opened them again, there was only a pile of empty ammunition boxes across the fire.
________________________________________
16:55
They heard on the radio that a Pamir village in the east had been bombed yesterday. More than a dozen people died, and many children were not found.
Someone scolded: "Bastard German." ”
He didn't speak. He suddenly wanted to ask: "Are you scolding Germans, or Russians, Americans, or Japanese?" ”
– or, are we ourselves?
Because they buried the explosives in advance, they hid the barracks, and they robbed the supplies. Before the village was flattened, was it because they had been hiding
there for the night?
He slammed into his feet and rushed out of the hole, trying to throw up. But I can't spit it out.
The stomach is empty, and so is the heart.
________________________________________
19:20
During the night, he had a dream.
In the dream, he went back to his childhood. My father washed clothes by the river, and my mother made bread in the house. He ran like a child, chasing a kite over stones,
grass and hillsides.
Suddenly, there was a loud bang, and he fell.
It's not him, it's the kite that broke the string and fell into the fire.
The kite is free.
He opened his eyes, and there was silence all around. He thought he was dead.
But he's still alive.
He sat up slowly, and there was only one sentence left in his head:
"What we have watered with blood is not freedom, but a deeper hell. May Allah have mercy on us. ”
________________________________________
21:10
The night was eerily quiet. He held the gun in his hand, and the barrel still had the body temperature of the Russian soldier - not the real temperature, the temperature
he imagined.
He fired a shot at the wall. Bullet casings hit the ground.
"Boom."
Hamid was startled and rushed over and asked, "What are you doing?" ”
He turned around and smiled on the verge of collapse:
"I just want to be sure...... We're not in Serrer..."

title: Meat grinder
desc:
The rubber edges of the gas mask pressed against Ivan Ivanovich Ivanov's cheek, and the exhaled white mist condensed into frost on the eyepiece. He cowered around the corner of the trench and listened to the distant sound of shelling, the rumbling sound, somehow, reminded him of the waterfall in his hometown...... Three months ago, he was fishing in the ice on the shores of Lake Baikal, but now he is huddled in the frozen soil of the highlands, which have been plowed countless times by the guns of the four countries, and he is tormented like hell.

"Rookie! Raise your gun high! "The stubble-faced platoon commander smashed Ivan's bulletproof vest with the butt of his rifle. The steel inserts hurt his ribs, and Ivan hurriedly raised the short assault rifle, and the condensed ice crystals on the barrel fell. Through the blackened snow, he saw a German Leopard tank engaged in a fierce exchange of fire with a Japanese Type 97 tank on the ridgeline 500 meters away...... I don't know which country's air raids left the craters, and there are still dark green oil stains.

Suddenly the radio burst out in shrill Russian: "Three o'clock direction!" Afghan maniac with RPG! Before Ivan could react, the trench he was in suddenly turned black - the dust kicked up by the rockets obscured the sky, and the cans and bullet casings that had been scattered on the ground flew around like pieces on an overturned chessboard. Suddenly, he felt some warm liquid spill into his neckline, and when he turned his head, it was the brain of Anthony, a veteran who had taught him to load magazines half an hour earlier. I saw that only half of Anthony's body was hanging from the sandbag, and the other half was gone. His intestines were steaming hot like thawed fish entrails, standing out in the gray-black dirt.

"Shoot! Shoot! The platoon commander's roar was mixed with the roar of a 12.7mm heavy machine gun. Ivan mechanically pulled the trigger. As the 5.45mm bullet passed through the falling snowflakes, the turbaned figure three hundred meters away exploded with blood in his chest. The man was killed instantly, but the bazooka in his hand was still launched, only to miss a lot, and smashed on an oil drum with the "Made in America" logo that had been left on the battlefield at some point, causing hundreds of more pieces of iron to the ground.

As night fell, Ivan huddled in a concrete bunker left behind by the Germans. The crack in the ventilation duct seeped into the minus 10 degrees Celsius cold, and the silence around him was enough to make him scared... He suddenly felt the slightly sharp bronze cross in his trouser pocket, which had been picked up from a blown up transport truck this morning, and its edges were covered with burn marks, and he felt a sense of silence as he looked at the small object that was faintly glowing with reddish-purple light.

At three o'clock in the morning, the shelling tore the night sky again. Ivan followed the assault team towards the pass, known to the Afghans as the "Valley of Blood," his boots creaking into the half-melted slush. Countless fireflies lit up in the darkness, and the Japanese Type 89 grenadiers and Russian AGS-17 grenade launchers roared at each other. At one point, Ivan saw a string of fresh footprints in the snow leading to the wreckage of a German-made Weasel armored vehicle, and he instinctively raised his gun to aim, even though he heard the cry of a newborn in the shadows — he knew that the fanatical Islamists would do anything. They use living people as bait, even babies, pregnant women, and even elderly people who have passed their old age...... Just as he was thinking, a pale-faced woman came out of the complete with the baby in her arms, and he immediately strengthened his vigilance and motioned for the other party to raise his hand. But the woman was unmoved, she smiled desolately, and pulled the safety bolt from her body with lightning speed, and Ivan now understood that it was too late. Blood flowers burst out of the woman's body, along with the high explosives strapped to her body. The last thing Ivan's consciousness remembered before falling into darkness was the shape of her mouth, even though he didn't know the Afghan language:
